title: Product Bulletin: Seasoned-Contract Free Percentage of a Corrected Partial-Withdrawal Charge, Deferred Fixed Annuities
content:
Annuity Product Management sets the free percentage of a corrected partial-withdrawal charge on Ashgrove Deferred Fixed Annuities contracts whose withdrawal fell late in the surrender charge schedule. The free percentage is the share of the contract value on the contract anniversary that opened the withdrawal's contract year (the initial premium in the first contract year) that is free of charge.

## Rule

The free percentage of a corrected partial-withdrawal charge is **15% (0.15)** where the annuitant was aged **70** or more on the contract anniversary that opened the withdrawal's contract year and the withdrawal fell in schedule year **4** or later, and **12% (0.12)** where the annuitant was under 70 on that anniversary and the withdrawal fell in schedule year 4 or later. Where the withdrawal fell in schedule year 3 or earlier, neither of these percentages applies, whatever the annuitant's age.

## Table

| Annuitant's age on the anniversary that opened the withdrawal's contract year | Schedule year in which the withdrawal fell | Free percentage under this bulletin |
|---|---|---|
| 70 or more | 4 or later | 15% |
| Under 70 | 4 or later | 12% |
| Any age | 1, 2 or 3 | Neither percentage applies |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

- Annuitant aged 70 on that anniversary, withdrawal in schedule year 4: 15%. Aged 69 on that anniversary, same withdrawal: 12%.
- An annuitant who turns 70 two months after that anniversary was 69 on it, so the 12% line governs for the rest of that contract year.
- Withdrawal in schedule year 3: neither percentage applies, at any age.
- With a contract value of $80000.00 on that anniversary, 15% makes $12000.00 of it free of charge and 12% makes $9600.00 free.

Ages are whole years last birthday from the annuitant's date of birth; schedule years run from the surrender charge schedule start date and contract years from the issue date and its anniversaries.
